_source.description: Global scandium production and development sites — one of the rarest critical minerals with no dedicated primary mines as of 2023
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); USGS Critical Minerals List 2022 (https://www.usgs.gov/news/national-news-release/us-geological-survey-releases-2022-list-critical-minerals); Scandium International Mining Corp technical reports and ASX filings; Clean TeQ/Sunrise Energy Metals NI 43-101 and ASX filings; Rio Tinto Fer et Titane corporate reports; Sumitomo Metal Mining annual reports; Rusal corporate disclosures; European Commission Critical Raw Materials assessments (https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/sectors/raw-materials/areas-specific-interest/critical-raw-materials_en)
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary of publicly reported production and project data
_source.notes: Scandium is produced at ~25-30 tonnes/year globally, almost entirely as byproduct. No dedicated primary scandium mines exist as of 2023. China dominates production (est. 10-15 tpa) from rare earth tailings, titanium slag processing, and red mud (alumina refining waste). Philippines is #2 via HPAL nickel laterite processing. Used in Al-Sc alloys for aerospace (lower welding requirements, higher strength), solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC), and high-intensity lighting. Several development-stage projects aim to increase supply. Coordinates from company filings, USGS, and satellite verification. USGS classifies scandium as a critical mineral.

_coverage.known_gaps: Several small Chinese titanium slag processors with scandium recovery not individually identified; Russian scandium recovery at Urals alumina plants; Vietnamese rare earth tailings processing; potential Ukrainian recovery operations whose current status is unclear due to conflict

sites.name: Bayan Obo REE Complex (Sc byproduct)
sites.operator: Baotou Steel / China Northern Rare Earth
sites.ownership: China Northern Rare Earth Group (state-owned, Inner Mongolia)
sites.type: open pit rare earth/iron ore (scandium byproduct from REE tailings)
sites.notes: World's largest rare earth deposit; Bayan Obo, Inner Mongolia; scandium recovered from REE processing tailings and residues; scandium is a trace component (~0.001% Sc2O3) in the carbonatite-hosted REE-iron ore; exact Sc production figures not publicly reported but China's Bayan Obo complex is believed to be the single largest source

sites.name: Guangxi Titanium Slag Processor (Sc recovery)
sites.notes: Scandium recovered from titanium tetrachloride production waste streams; Nanning area, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; multiple small-scale operations extracting Sc from TiCl4 process residues; exact facilities not individually disclosed

sites.name: Sichuan Titanium/REE Scandium Recovery
sites.notes: Scandium recovered from Panzhihua titanium-vanadium magnetite processing residues; Panzhihua, Sichuan Province; the Panzhihua deposit contains ~0.003% Sc2O3; recovery from blast furnace slag and titanium processing waste

sites.name: Rusal Alumina Refinery (Sc from red mud)
sites.type: alumina refinery (scandium from bauxite residue/red mud)
sites.notes: Pilot-to-commercial scandium recovery from red mud (bauxite residue) at Rusal's Ural Alumina Refinery, Kamensk-Uralsky area; Rusal has developed proprietary technology to extract scandium oxide from alumina production waste; reported ~3 tpa Sc2O3 capacity; red mud typically contains 50-100 ppm Sc

sites.name: Taganito HPAL Plant (THPAL)
sites.ownership: Sumitomo Metal Mining (majority, JV with Nickel Asia Corporation)
sites.type: high-pressure acid leach nickel laterite (scandium byproduct)
sites.notes: Scandium recovered as byproduct of HPAL nickel-cobalt processing; Claver, Surigao del Norte, Mindanao; Sumitomo developed proprietary scandium extraction from HPAL intermediate product; one of the world's largest scandium producers; nickel laterite ore contains ~50 ppm Sc

sites.name: Coral Bay Nickel (HPAL)
sites.ownership: Sumitomo Metal Mining (majority, JV with Rio Tuba Nickel Mining Corp/Nickel Asia)
sites.type: high-pressure acid leach nickel laterite (scandium potential)
sites.notes: HPAL nickel processing at Rio Tuba, Palawan; scandium recovery from nickel laterite processing; sister plant to Taganito THPAL; Sumitomo exploring expanded Sc recovery capacity

sites.name: Dalur ISR Uranium (Sc byproduct)
sites.ownership: Rosatom State Corporation (via ARMZ Uranium Holding/Dalur)
sites.type: in-situ recovery uranium (scandium byproduct from leach solution)
sites.notes: Scandium recovered as byproduct from uranium in-situ recovery (ISR) leach solutions; Dalmatovsky district, Kurgan Oblast, western Siberia; Dalur extracts scandium from pregnant leach solutions that contain dissolved Sc from host sandstones; small but consistent producer

sites.name: Zheltye Vody (Zhovti Vody) Scandium Facility
sites.type: scandium recovery from uranium processing residues
sites.notes: Former Soviet-era scandium production facility; Zhovti Vody, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast; historically produced Sc2O3 from uranium processing waste; operational status uncertain since 2022 due to Russian invasion of Ukraine; located in central Ukraine, not in active combat zone but supply chains disrupted; was one of the world's few dedicated scandium producers

sites.name: Syerston/Scandium21 (Sunrise Project)
sites.ownership: Sunrise Energy Metals Ltd (ASX listed; formerly Clean TeQ Holdings)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest known scandium resources; Fifield area, central-western New South Wales; laterite deposit with ~430 ppm Sc average grade; DFS completed; planned capacity 20 tpa Sc2O3 plus nickel/cobalt; awaiting financing/FID; would be world's first large-scale primary scandium operation if built

sites.name: Nyngan Scandium Project
sites.operator: Scandium International Mining Corp (now NiCo Resources)
sites.ownership: Scandium International Mining Corp (TSX listed; rebranded as NiCo Resources)
sites.notes: Dedicated scandium project near Nyngan, central-western New South Wales; laterite-hosted scandium with grades ~235 ppm Sc; DFS completed 2016; EPA approved; planned as world's first dedicated primary scandium mine; 38 tpa Sc2O3 capacity in Phase 1; seeking financing

sites.name: Rio Tinto RTFT — Sorel-Tracy (Sc from TiO2 waste)
sites.type: titanium dioxide/iron processing (scandium from waste streams)
sites.notes: Scandium recovery from titanium dioxide and steel production waste streams; Sorel-Tracy, Quebec; Rio Tinto developed proprietary scandium extraction technology from acid waste (scandium contained in Sorel ilmenite smelting residues); commissioned 2021; part of Rio Tinto's 'AtlasSc' critical minerals initiative; processes ilmenite from Havre-Saint-Pierre mine

sites.name: REEtec Scandium Recovery (Herøya)
sites.type: rare earth separation plant with scandium recovery
sites.notes: REE separation facility under development at Herøya Industrial Park, Porsgrunn, Norway; plans to recover scandium alongside rare earth separation; using proprietary RE-LIXIR technology; feedstock from various REE concentrate sources; part of European critical raw materials supply chain diversification effort

sites.name: Pavlodar Alumina Refinery (Sc potential)
sites.type: alumina refinery (scandium from bauxite residue — potential)
sites.notes: Potential scandium recovery from bauxite residue (red mud) at Pavlodar alumina refinery; Pavlodar, northeastern Kazakhstan; ERG has explored scandium extraction from accumulated red mud stockpiles; Kazakh bauxite residues reported to contain 60-120 ppm Sc; production scale uncertain — likely small pilot quantities

sites.name: JXTG/ENEOS Scandium Recovery
sites.ownership: ENEOS Holdings (publicly listed, Tokyo Stock Exchange)
sites.notes: Pilot-scale scandium recovery from nickel processing waste at ENEOS facilities; Yamaguchi Prefecture area; ENEOS has developed technology to extract Sc from nickel smelter waste; partnering with Sumitomo Metal Mining on Sc supply chain; Japan's SOFC fuel cell industry is key Sc demand driver

sites.name: Sumitomo Metal Mining — Niihama Sc Refining
sites.ownership: Sumitomo Metal Mining (publicly listed, Tokyo Stock Exchange; Sumitomo Group)
sites.notes: Scandium oxide purification and refining at Niihama, Ehime Prefecture; processes scandium-bearing intermediate from Philippine HPAL operations (Taganito, Coral Bay); Sumitomo is vertically integrated from nickel laterite mining to Sc2O3 purification; supplies Japanese SOFC manufacturers

sites.name: Platina Scandium Project (Owendale)
sites.notes: Scandium-cobalt-nickel-platinum laterite deposit near Owendale, central-western New South Wales; PFS completed; scandium grade ~575 ppm Sc in high-grade zone; planned 10 tpa Sc2O3; seeking offtake and financing; located in same laterite belt as Syerston and Nyngan projects

sites.name: Scandium Canada (Crater Lake project)
sites.notes: Crater Lake scandium project in northern Quebec; one of the highest-grade primary scandium deposits globally (~359 ppm Sc2O3); carbonatite-hosted; PEA completed; remote location on Ungava Peninsula; would require significant infrastructure investment; advanced exploration/PEA stage

sites.name: Yermakovskoye Deposit (Sc reserve)
sites.notes: Significant scandium deposit in Buryatia, eastern Siberia; one of the world's largest known scandium resources; iron-scandium bearing ores with ~0.05% Sc2O3; development proposed multiple times but not advanced; remote location; included in Russian strategic mineral reserve estimates; current development status unclear
